title: Multi-Task Learning Using Uncertainty to Weigh Losses for Scene Geometry and Semantics
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
problem_statement: Multi-task deep learning performance is highly sensitive to manual relative weighting of task losses with different scales and units (e.g., meters vs. classification logits), making naive weighted sums w_i L_i expensive to tune by grid search and prohibitive for real-time scene understanding where geometry and semantics must be learned jointly.
domain: Computer Vision — monocular scene understanding with joint pixel-wise depth regression, semantic segmentation, and instance segmentation from a single RGB image for real-time robotics
theoretical_framework: Probabilistic homoscedastic (task-dependent) uncertainty where observation noise σ captures task noise independent of input; maximizing Gaussian likelihood for regression and scaled softmax (Boltzmann/temperature) likelihood for classification yields principled weighting terms 1/(2σ²) L + log σ that automatically balance losses.
methodology: Derivation of multi-task likelihood factorizing p(y1,…,yK|f^W(x)) = ∏ p(y_k|f^W(x)) and negative log-likelihood. For two regressions: L = 1/(2σ1²)||y1-f||² + 1/(2σ2²)||y2-f||² + log σ1σ2. For classification: scaled softmax p(y=c|f,σ)=Softmax(1/σ² f) giving L ≈ 1/σ² CE + log σ via approximation Σ exp(1/σ² f) ≈ (Σ exp f)^{1/σ²}. Combined regression+classification: L(W,σ1,σ2) ≈ 1/(2σ1²)L1 + 1/σ2² L2 + log σ1 + log σ2, trained by regressing log variance s=log σ² for numerical stability. Architecture uses ResNet101 + ASPP encoder (DeepLabV3, output stride 8) shared across tasks followed by task-specific decoders (3×3 conv 256 + 1×1 output): cross-entropy for semantic segmentation, L1 on instance centroid vectors x̂_n with OPTICS clustering for instance segmentation, and L1 on metric inverse depth (sky set to zero) for depth, averaging losses over labelled pixels per batch.
datasets: CityScapes — 2,975 training and 500 validation stereo images at 2048×1024 (train downsampled to 128×256 and 256×512 for ablations, full resolution for benchmark), with 20-class semantic labels, instance masks for 8 instance classes, disparity from SGM stereo treated as pseudo inverse-depth ground truth (22 cm baseline, fine weather cities), 1,525 test images held out for online server

metrics: Semantic segmentation: mean Intersection over Union (IoU class and category, higher better) and instance-weighted IoU
Instance segmentation: mean pixel error between predicted and ground-truth instance centroid vectors [px], and Average Precision AP, AP50%, AP100m, AP50m
Depth: mean error [px] and RMS error [px] on inverse depth versus SGM disparity
Weight robustness and training dynamics: loss weight trajectories and sensitivity to initialization
baselines: Single-task models trained individually for each of the three tasks
Approximately optimal grid-searched weights (0.89 semantic, 0.01 instance, 0.1 depth on Tiny CityScapes)
Pairwise task combinations with uncertainty weighting (2-task) versus all three tasks (3-task)
State-of-the-art single-task specialists: Uhrig et al. for semantic+instance, Mask R-CNN, Deep Watershed, R-CNN+MCG for instance only, DeepLabV3, PSPNet, Adelaide for semantic only
architectures: ResNet101 + ASPP shared encoder (DeepLabV3) plus task-specific decoders, compared under identical encoder capacity; ablations at 128×256 over 50k iterations, final benchmark at full 1024×2048

key_findings: Naive uniform weighting (0.333 each) degrades semantic IoU to 50.1% below single-task 59.4%, while learned uncertainty weighting on all three tasks improves to 63.4% IoU, 3.50 px instance error, and 0.522 mean inverse depth error, outperforming single-task models on all tasks.

Approximate grid-searched optimal weights (62.8% IoU, 0.549 depth error) are still inferior to learned 3-task uncertainty weighting (63.4%, 0.522), because uncertainty weights are dynamic during training (final ratio 43:1:0.16 for semantic:depth:instance) and not limited by search grid resolution, with uncertainty steadily decreasing during training.

Figure 2 demonstrates that at optimal manual weighting the joint model beats separate models, but nearby weightings degrade one task; uncertainty weighting automatically finds that optimum without expensive search and is robust to initialization, converging in a few hundred iterations.

Two-task uncertainty models already beat single tasks (e.g., semantic+depth 62.7% IoU / 0.533 depth versus 59.4% single), and three-task joint learning further improves over any pair, showing complementary regularization: depth cues help segmentation smoothness and vice versa.

On CityScapes test benchmark at full resolution, the single unified model achieves 78.5 class IoU / 57.4 instance-weighted IoU / 89.9 category IoU and performs competitively on instance and depth (77.7 category iIoU, 21.6 AP) while being the first to address all three tasks jointly in real time, reducing computation versus three separate models.
scope_and_delimitations: Evaluated exclusively on CityScapes road scenes (German cities, fine weather, same sensor) at 128×256 for ablations and 1024×2048 for benchmark, not on indoor NYU, Mapillary, or non-vision domains.

Jointly learned only three tasks with fixed definitions (semantic cross-entropy, instance centroid L1 with OPTICS clustering, inverse depth L1 with sky zero) and not surface normals, optical flow, or other classifications.
Compared only uniform, grid-searched, and homoscedastic uncertainty weightings; did not compare to later gradient-based methods (GradNorm, PCGrad, CAGrad) which postdate this work.
Assumed homoscedastic (input-independent) uncertainty and factorized likelihood across tasks, ignoring heteroscedastic per-pixel uncertainty and task correlations.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: There are many interesting questions left unanswered. Firstly, our results show that there is usually not a single optimal weighting for all tasks. Therefore, what is the optimal weighting? Is multitask learning is an ill-posed optimisation problem without a single higher-level goal?
limitations.summary: Authors acknowledge that multitask weighting may lack a single optimal solution and pose multitask learning as potentially ill-posed without a higher-level objective; they also raise open questions about optimal encoder/decoder split depth and why certain task pairs (semantics+depth) outperform others, without providing those answers.

generalizability_gap: No evaluation on code-switched, multilingual, or low-resource text, on indoor scenes, or on transformer-based language models; homoscedastic weighting not tested outside geometry+semantics vision tasks or on noisy user-generated data, limiting claims for disaster tweet, code-switch, or NLP multi-task settings surveyed elsewhere in this repository.
methodological_gap: Homoscedastic uncertainty captures only task-dependent constant noise, not input-dependent heteroscedastic noise, task relationships, or gradient conflicts; the softmax temperature scaling relies on approximation Σ exp(1/σ² f) ≈ (Σ exp f)^{1/σ²} which is exact only as σ→1, and instance segmentation relies on separate OPTICS clustering post-processing rather than end-to-end learning, with depth evaluated against noisy SGM pseudo ground truth rather than LiDAR.
future_work: Investigating whether a single optimal weighting exists or whether multitask learning is inherently ill-posed without a higher-level objective.
Determining optimal shared encoder depth and split point into task-specific decoders for balancing shared versus task-specific capacity.
Quantifying task relationships to predict which task combinations are complementary for representation learning.
